chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"If a mu'adhdhin repeats the Shahadah, and the 'Hayya 'ala al-Salah' or 'Hayya 'ala al-Falah' twice, three times, or more than that, when he is an Imam who wishes to gather the people to assemble them, there is no harm in it."
Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: So when he finishes his Adhan as we explained, he should sit after it with a light sit until he says: 'When he intends to establish the Iqamah.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to repeat the Adhan phrases multiple times to gather the congregation?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the flexibility in the Adhan’s structure, permitting the Mu'adhdhin to repeat the Shahadah and 'Hayya' phrases multiple times specifically for the purpose of gathering the congregation. Al-Sheikh’s appended note highlights the practical etiquette of pausing briefly after the Adhan to allow for transition before the Iqamah, reflecting the juristic emphasis on facilitating communal worship. This ruling underscores the principle of *ease* (taysir) in ritual calls when the primary objective is the assembly of the faithful.
